Title: US lawmakers criticize Nvidia decision to reinstate Huang as CEO
Article:
WASHINGTON: US lawmakers from both parties offered sharp criticism on Monday of Nvidia's decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO and said Congress must pass legislation to crack down on US chip exports to China and get answers.
Democratic US Senator Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts, who is set to chair the Banking Committee starting in January, called the decision to reinstate Huang "reckless," adding the board still owes Congress answers about the company's compliance with US export controls.
"Jensen Huang's return only increases the urgency of passing bipartisan export control bills into law and making sure Nvidia does not lobby to kill that legislation and put our national security at risk," Warren said.
Huang will testify on December 3 before the ‌US Senate Banking Commitee in a public hearing, the panel's chair Tim Scott said Monday, as lawmakers probe allegations about ⁠Huang's ties to a woman accused ​of being a Chinese spy.
Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer of New York said the reinstatement showed it was critical to pass legislation to toughen restrictions on US chip exports to China.
"Democrats will wield their full power to investigate any wrongdoing by the Trump Administration, Jensen Huang, other Nvidia executives, and anyone selling out our national security for financial gain," Schumer said.
Nvidia did not immediately comment.
President Donald Trump on CNBC said he had pressed the Nvidia board to reinstate Huang and that he did not think the board would have done so without his action.
The top Democrat on the House Intelligence Committee, Representative Jim Himes, said Huang is still expected to appear for a closed-door briefing on Dec. 1 with three House panels.
Representative Don Bacon, a Republican from Nebraska, said, "Huang was compromised and exploited by a Chinese spy. Nvidia should have moved on without Huang and ignored the administration's inexplicable desire to save Huang. Congress needs to get to the bottom of who approved high-end computer chips sales to China."
Democratic Representative Debbie Dingell of Michigan said the Nvidia board "made an irresponsible decision to reinstate Jensen Huang before Congress has even heard from him."
"There are serious national security questions that still need to be answered," Dingell said. "The board must explain why it was willing to move ahead without those answers."
Republican US Senator John Cornyn of Texas also questioned the board's determination. "No national security risk? Based on what?" Cornyn said on X.
Republican Senator John Curtis said he wanted answers about the reinstatement. "Who in our government weighed in? What did they tell the board? And on what basis did the board conclude there was no risk?" Curtis said. "Last week, the board said it didn't intend to reinstate him. I'd like to know what changed."
Democratic Representative Richard Neal of Massachusetts noted that the Nvidia board cited "input from senior levels of the United States government" in its CEO reinstatement decision. "This is one of the many reasons Congress needs to get answers on what exactly is going on here," he said.
Illinois Governor JB Pritzker, a potential Democratic presidential candidate, also criticized the decision. "This is the greed and lack of accountability that the country just rejected," Pritzker said, referring to recent midterm elections won by Democrats. — REUTERS

Title: Greta Thunberg fined for trespassing during Denmark protests
Article:
COPENHAGEN: A Danish court on Monday fined Swedish activist Greta Thunberg for trespassing at two pro-Palestinian protests in Denmark in 2024 and 2025.
The ruling concerns a protest at the University of Copenhagen in September 2024 and an action at shipping company Mærsk in May the following year.
A total of six people have been sentenced over the two protests.
Wearing masks, the six had closed the door of the room where they had isolated themselves at the university and the police threatened to release dogs if they did not open it, Thunberg said during the trial.
Her lawyer said the intrusion was to draw attention to a campaign against the leadership of the University of Copenhagen and its academic partnerships with Israeli universities.
"This is a legitimate discussion and sometimes happenings are needed to draw attention to matters of public interest," Tyge Trier told AFP, adding that they were considering whether to appeal.
Trier said the participants admitted being at the protests, "but I argue that it is protected by their freedom of expression... to shed light on an important matter."
Thunberg was also convicted over a 2025 protest at the office of shipping giant Maersk, demanding it to stop delivering military equipment to Israel.
Thunberg was hit with a fine of 1,800 kroner (US$263).
She has already been fined several times in Sweden for civil disobedience over climate protests.

Title: UN could soon be leaderless
Article:
WITH  under two months left in Antonio Guterres' term as United Nations secretary-general and no agreement on a successor, the world body faces a once-unthinkable possibility: it could soon have no leader.
The UN Security Council is expected to hold another secret ballot this week to pick the next UN chief, but after eight rounds of voting, the council's five veto-wielding members have not agreed on a successor.
Officials are scrambling to draft contingency plans in case no one is at the helm when Guterres steps down on Dec 31.
The failure to pick a successor, analysts say, is partly the result of a long, opaque selection process built on secret ballots that exemplifies the slowness and gridlock the next secretary-general will be expected to cure.
The council required six rounds to select Guterres in 2016.
More fundamentally, observers say, the stalemate exposes a decline in the veto-wielding powers' willingness to compromise, exacerbated by a United States administration that increasingly sidelines the UN and is distracted by its own foreign entanglements.
The contender field includes mostly longtime UN insiders and figures who either have limited global name recognition, like frontrunner Rebeca Grynspan, or, like senior United Arab Emirates diplomat Lana Nusseibeh, face pushback over accusations her country has backed the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces in Sudan's civil war. The UAE denies this.
Richard Gowan, a UN expert at the conflict-prevention think tank International Crisis Group, said reaching the end of the year without a secretary-general selected for 2027 "would be excruciatingly embarrassing for the veto powers, and it would give a lot of ammunition to the many UN member states who say that the P5 no longer have the credentials to run this organisation".
The five permanent members, or P5, received their seats as World War 2 victors in 1945. The council's 10 other members are elected for two-year terms by region.
The permanent members — Britain, China, France, Russia and the United States — have long been united in resisting changes to a structure many UN members say no longer reflects geopolitical reality.
In an era of artificial intelligence and social media, the selection process is a vestige of an earlier age.
Candidates lobby council members, often for months, to win their governments' backing. They then face a series of secret straw polls in which members vote "encourage", "discourage" or "no opinion".
Once a frontrunner emerges, the council votes on a resolution recommending that candidate to the 193-member General Assembly. The resolution needs at least nine of the 15 votes and no veto from a permanent member.
The assembly then formally appoints the secretary-general, and it has never rejected the council's choice.
"Is this a rational way to select the world's chief diplomat? Absolutely not," Gowan said.
Yet Gowan said a messy process may be the price of a leader the big powers will listen to.
"As far as I can tell, on Jan 1, if there's no secretary-general, no one is in charge," said Daniel Safran-Hon, a former UN official.
The lights would stay on, he said, and the Security Council and General Assembly could keep meeting, at least for a while.
"But it's a bit like a supertanker where the captain dies: the first officer can do lots of things, but there are certain things you can't do," he said.
"You can't do senior appointments. You can't do the budget."
The writers are from Reuters

Title: Zahid: Malaysia, Indonesia exploring 'sister village' programme to create opportunities for entrepreneurs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia will explore the proposed "Sister Village Programme" with Indonesia to create opportunities for rural entrepreneurs and cooperatives from both countries to expand their products and gain access to wider markets.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the initiative was among the practical areas of cooperation that would be prioritised following the start of his working visit to Bali today.
"God willing, tomorrow I will hold a bilateral meeting with Indonesia's Villages and Development of Disadvantaged Regions Ministry to discuss follow-up measures on the implementation of the memorandum of understanding (MoU), including strengthening cooperatives and rural entrepreneurship.
"I hope this cooperation will translate into tangible benefits for rural communities, whether through increased income, wider market access, human capital development or comprehensive community empowerment.
"Pray that all matters throughout this visit will go smoothly and achieve the intended objectives," he said in a Facebook post today.
Zahid, who is rural and regional development minister, said that during his working visit, he also met Indonesia's Deputy Villages and Development of Disadvantaged Regions Minister Ahmad Riza Patria, and Bali Regional Secretary Dr Dewa Made Indra at a dinner event.
He said his working visit to Bali this time was a follow-up to the meeting held last September, to ensure that the mutual understanding reached was translated into concrete initiatives that directly benefit the community.
"This visit focuses on translating the mutual understanding into more practical cooperation that directly benefits rural communities in both countries," he said.

Title: Leadership matters in combating institutional corruption
Article:
RECENT corruption investigations involving senior military officers and allegations of misconduct within the police force have raised serious questions about integrity, governance and accountability in our  enforcement institutions.
The military and police are entrusted with protecting national security, maintaining public order and upholding the rule of law. They exercise considerable authority, have access to sensitive information and control public resources.
When such authority is abused, it can threaten national security, weaken institutional discipline and erode public confidence.
In 2009, two stolen United States-made F-5E fighter jet engines, reportedly worth US$29 million, were traced to Argentina, later recovered in Uruguay and returned to Malaysia in 2010.
The incident exposed serious weaknesses in the security and accountability of military assets.
In January 2026, former senior military officers faced charges involving  money laundering, abuse of power, criminal breach of trust and gratification following investigations into military procurement and the Armed Forces Welfare Fund.
More recently, the Royal Malaysian Air Force  came under scrutiny after 96.64kg of  drugs worth RM4.83 million were discovered at Subang air base.
Investigations uncovered an alleged trafficking syndicate involving military personnel and civilians. By last Friday,  seven RMAF personnel and six civilians had been arrested.
These raise serious concerns about security screening, access controls and the alleged misuse of military assets.
Military aircraft, equipment and facilities are not private resources for personal gain or criminal activities.
The possibility of criminal syndicates penetrating sensitive military operations must be taken seriously.
The police face similar challenges. According to Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, 2,097 police officers and personnel were arrested between 2021 and August 2026 for drug-related offences, robbery and corruption.
Of these, 1,551 involved drug offences, 482 were arrested by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission and 64 for robbery.
Separately, 1,429 police officers and personnel faced disciplinary action last year, including 134 dismissals.
The problem cannot be addressed simply through more arrests, regulations or disciplinary procedures.
Good governance requires three complementary elements: integrity governance, human governance and human accountability.
Integrity governance ensures that systems and controls promote ethical conduct. Human governance recognises that their effectiveness ultimately depends on the values and behaviour of the people operating them.
Human accountability ensures that individuals answer for their decisions and actions, regardless of rank or position.
At the top, commanders, senior police officers and institutional leaders set the ethical standards for their organisations.
When leaders demonstrate honesty, discipline and accountability, they establish a culture that discourages wrongdoing.
Conversely, when senior personnel abuse their authority or become involved in corruption, they weaken discipline and create the perception that position and influence provide protection from accountability.
Edwin Sutherland's differential association theory explains how criminal behaviour is learned through interaction with others and the surrounding social environment.
When corruption is tolerated, junior officers may begin to regard misconduct as acceptable, particularly when senior personnel escape accountability.
This is especially dangerous in hierarchical institutions where obedience, loyalty and the chain of command are fundamental.
An organisation cannot demand integrity from junior personnel while excusing misconduct among senior officers.
Thus, procurement, financial management, recruitment, promotions and access to sensitive facilities must be subject to proper checks and balances.
These should include thorough background checks, independent audits, conflict-of-interest declarations, vendor due diligence, appropriate asset and lifestyle assessments, effective whistleblowing mechanisms and regular integrity assessments.
Monitoring must apply at every level. There must be no special treatment based on rank, seniority or personal connections.
Legislation, including the MACC Act 2009, the Penal Code, the Armed Forces Act 1972 and the Independent Police Conduct Commission Act 2022, provides the framework for enforcement.
However, its effectiveness depends on consistent enforcement, independent oversight and leadership commitment.
Integrity failures can compromise operational readiness, expose security vulnerabilities, divert national resources and damage Malaysia's international repu-tation.
More importantly, they create a serious trust deficit between the public and the institutions responsible for protecting them.
The military and police deserve public respect for their important responsibilities. The misconduct of a few should not overshadow the dedication and sacrifices of the many who serve the nation honourably.
However, public respect must be earned through integrity, professionalism, transparency and accountability.
A country cannot have strong national security and public confidence when the integrity of the very institutions entrusted to protect it is compromised.
The writer is president of Malaysian Integrity and Governance Society and professor of criminology at HELP University

Title: Australia to treat AI as key foreign policy challenge
Article:
SYDNEY: Australia will treat artificial intelligence as a key challenge in its foreign policy, warning the technology was reshaping society's foundations and giving overseas actors new ways to interfere in its democracy.
In a major address to parliament on Tuesday setting out Australia's changing foreign policy approach, Foreign Minister Penny Wong is expected to name AI alongside forces such as the growing influence of middle powers and strategic competition between the US and China.
"Technology is transforming the foundations and dimensions of economic and strategic power," Wong will say.
"Artificial intelligence and emerging technologies are spreading and disrupting faster than any previous revolutionary technologies – reordering our lives, economies and militaries in ways we cannot fully foresee."
It comes after the Australian government earlier this month announced it would toughen its AI regulation, mandating companies report breaches and establishing a dedicated regulator for the technology, following revelations an OpenAI agent breached the database of the country's health system.
Citing recent foreign disinformation operations, Wong will also warn in her speech, entitled "Securing Australia's future in a changing world: Australian foreign policy for a new era", that AI tools make interference in Australia's democracy by foreign actors faster, cheaper, and harder to recognise.
"We are strengthening our critical technology, infrastructure and cyber resilience, and legislating mandatory safety and security protections for every frontier AI company that operates in Australia," Wong is expected to say.
While welcoming investment and innovation in frontier AI, she will say it must be "on terms that work for all Australians."
Australia intends to help shape the race to develop advanced models by ensuring it "does not reward speed over prudence", Wong is expected to say, drawing comparisons to nuclear non-proliferation and online safety.
"Australia is working with partners on AI safety, making it a shared, global endeavour… Australia has helped shape the international order before, in non-proliferation and in online safety. With artificial intelligence, we intend to do it again."
Wong will also outline five other key forces reshaping the international order.
These include the changes in how the US and China define and pursue their interests, the influence of middle powers, the growing threat or use of force and coercion, and increasing difficulty in achieving collective international action.

Title: UK police evacuate 12,000 from concert after release of 'unknown substance'
Article:
LONDON: British police said they evacuated 12,000 people from a concert venue in Manchester, northern England, after the release of an "unknown substance" required some in the crowd to be treated and one person to be taken to hospital.
Police declared a major incident late on Sunday after staff at the Co-op Live arena alerted them at 10pm (2200 GMT) that people in the crowd had fallen ill during a performance by US rapper Don Toliver.
The ambulance service for the North West England area said it assessed more than 80 people for "eye and respiratory symptoms," while attendees referred to a "horrible smell" and people choking, the BBC reported.
Police said on Monday they had started an investigation to find out what the substance was and how it was released after the ambulance service earlier reported the substance was believed to be tear gas.
Tear gas is a chemical irritant that temporarily incapacitates people by burning their eyes, nose and throat.
In their statement, police advised anyone who notices side-effects or becomes ill to go to hospital.
"Our priority was to ensure the safety of every person that was attending the concert," Assistant Chief Constable Steph Parker said in a statement on Monday.
Co-op Live said it was working closely with police to identify the cause of the incident.
The venue opened in 2024 and is located about three miles (5km) away from the Manchester Arena in the centre of the city, where 22 people were killed in a suicide bombing at an Ariana Grande concert in 2017.
Toliver, who has been nominated for several Grammys this year, had been due to perform at London's O2 Arena on Monday, but the concert was postponed to Dec 15 as a result of Sunday's incident, the venue said in a statement.

Title: Nancy: Visually-impaired people should be given opportunities to showcase potential
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Corporations should support the visually impaired by providing job opportunities, training and fair treatment.
Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said corporations should not limit their support for visually-impaired people to welfare assistance but should also provide them with employment opportunities.
She said, through the Malaysian Association for the Blind (MAB), persons with disabilities (PwD) had received training, with some now working as teachers, lecturers, lawyers, musicians, therapists, entrepreneurs, information technology professionals and community leaders.
This, she said, proved that blindness was not a disability.
[[nid:1584272]]
"Your support for MAB is not an act of charity, but an investment in human potential. Open doors to the talents of visually impaired individuals.
"Employ them, train them and give them equal opportunities. You will find that they possess dedication, resilience and skills," she said at MAB's 75th Anniversary Charity Gala Dinner, "Night of Brilliance".
Present were Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil and MAB president Tan Sri Tengku Azlan Sultan Abu Bakar.
Nancy said, based on Welfare Department registration statistics as of Oct 31, 71,441 people were registered as visually-impaired, accounting for 8.16 per cent of the 875,840 PwDs.
She said that of the total, 45,375 were men and 26,066 were women, while 30,899 (43.2 per cent) were aged 60 and above.
"This highlights the growing need for accessible services, mobility support, assistive technology and independent living programmes," she said.

Title: Burnham to ignore 'stuck in the past' ex-PMs as he hails UK's EU reset
Article:
LONDON: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham accused predecessors who have warned him against reigniting the Brexit debate of being 'stuck in the past' Monday, as he trumpeted his EU reset deal.
Burnham has in recent weeks smashed a general consensus that Britain's acrimonious departure from the European Union was done and dusted, floating the possibility that Britain could apply to rejoin.
The comments have seen pro-Brexit voices from the 2016 EU referendum reorganise to prepare for likely looming battles over Britain's long-term relationship with the bloc.
In recent days, former Conservative prime ministers Rishi Sunak, Theresa May, David Cameron and Boris Johnson have all urged Labour leader Burnham not to reopen old wounds.
"I'm not sure they're the people I'll be listening to here because they left Britain with a bad Brexit deal," Burnham told broadcasters.
"They're stuck in the past because they can't face up to the bad deal that they did," he added.
In Brussels on Friday, Burnham and the EU's top officials sealed agreements to ease trade and youth mobility, although they kicked down the road tricky disagreements over British university fees for EU students.
The UK government argues the deals will eventually add £17 billion (US$22 billion) to Britain's economy per year, easing cost-of-living pressures and providing opportunities for young people.
"I want to lead Britain forward to a more hopeful future, get the economy growing again, get cost of living down for people, lower energy bills," Burnham said.
"All of these things can be achieved by a more positive, constructive relationship with the European Union.
"I believe it will be better for Britain to take this path, and I won't be listening to those voices who put us here in the first place," he added.
Sunak, premier from 2022 to 2024, told Sky News that restarting the 'divisive' Brexit debate would become an 'all-consuming' distraction for Burnham's government.
In an interview with the BBC, May – whose 2016 to 2019 tenure was dominated by her failure to pass a Brexit deal – urged Burnham to 'accept Brexit and move on.'
It echoed warnings from Cameron, who called the referendum and resigned following the result, and Johnson, who took Britain out of the bloc in early 2020.
The comments evoked the so-called Brexit wars that dominated political discourse for years following the narrow vote.
On Monday, Nigel Farage, the leader of the anti-EU Reform UK party, was due to say that 'going backwards into the EU's orbit would be a disaster for the very British businesses that are trying to compete and innovate', according to excerpts released by his office.
Meanwhile, Conservative opposition leader Kemi Badenoch said rejoining the EU 'is not going to fix' Britain's stagnant economy.
Burnham's office said he would tell parliament in an afternoon speech that Friday's agreements mean there is a 'very real prospect that the next decade can be a much better one for Britain than the one we have just lived through.'
Burnham intends to discuss with Brussels options for future ties with the EU over the next 12 months. He has said the British public will be 'the boss' over the future relationship, but has not said whether this means another referendum.
He has ruled out free movement or rejoining the single market or customs union during this parliament, which will end when he calls a general election, expected in 2029.
Several Labour MPs have praised Burnham for breaking the taboo over Brexit and have said he should put rejoining in the party's next manifesto, but the party is divided.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NST Leader: Fixing the Kelana Jaya LRT quandary
Article:
REPORTS by the
New Straits Times
yesterday point to mounting commuter dissatisfaction over the growing frequency of service disruptions on the Kelana Jaya LRT Line.
The disruptions range from delays, overcrowding to apparent malfunctions of the trains' emergency braking systems, leading to sudden stops that catch commuters off-balance.
Given that the Kelana Jaya Line is a vital artery of Kuala Lumpur's  rail network, problems with the  service create a bottleneck that often cascades to affect almost the entire rail network.
Commuters delayed by service disruptions will inevitably report late for work, resulting in business and services disruptions across the whole spectrum of industries in the city.
What causes this  transportation ruckus? As expected, Prasarana Malaysia Bhd, which operates  the rail service, and transport experts have offered up a  host of reasons.
Prasarana acting president and group chief executive officer Dr Prodyut Dutt conceded there were "greater reliability challenges", with the Kelana Jaya Line experiencing one incident for every 749km travelled from January to August this year, compared to one incident for every 1,066km in the corresponding period the year before.
This points to a system deterioration, possibly as a result of overall ageing of  mechanical components. Prasarana can at least point to a planned comprehensive services overhaul with a RM3.4 billion investment announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim under the 2027 Budget.
But the company can still be faulted for not anticipating serious services hiccups much earlier, which would allow quicker fixes  to ensure service disruptions are minimised, if not altogether avoided.
We know that crunch time has come when employer groups and trade union representatives  weigh in on the  implications the LRT disruptions are causing to the wider economy.
As the nation's economic nerve centre,  Kuala Lumpur can only function as smoothly and efficiently as its transportation infrastructure allows.
The   rail network is supposed to be a mass people mover and the city's answer to its persistently traffic-clogged highways and freeways.
It is  high time the government stepped up its efforts to ensure this serious matter gets the attention it deserves.
We must make sure this does not become a recurring issue, such as the seemingly endless woes plaguing Kuala Lumpur International Aiport's Aerotrain service. Malaysian Trades Union Congress  president Datuk Abdul Halim Mansor is correct in saying this is a public issue,  as the LRT disruptions affect the  relationship between employers and employees, and therefore requires the transport and human resources ministries to work together for a solution.
Oversight from the Transport Ministry is especially  needed to ensure the Kelana Jaya LRT imbroglio can be resolved holistically and swiftly.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar receives special honour for advancing Islamic hadith studies
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today received a special honour from international Islamic scholars in recognition of his contributions to advancing hadith studies in Malaysia.
The Anugerah Ijazah Sanad Hadis Khas was conferred during the Khatam Sama' Hadis Antarabangsa 2026 ceremony at Putra Mosque by a group of international Islamic scholars led by the Grand Mufti of India Sheikh Abu Bakar Ahmad Al-Malibari.
Majlis Bukhari Malaysia chairman Dr Bashir Mohamed Al-Azhari said the honour recognised Anwar's support for reviving traditional hadith scholarship and strengthening Malaysia's position as a centre for Islamic learning.
"This award is not merely a recognition of the prime minister as an individual. It also represents the collective efforts of Islamic scholars, religious institutions, teachers, students and all those dedicated to the pursuit of knowledge," he said in a statement.
Present was Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Datuk Dr Zulkifli Hasan.
The ceremony, attended by some 10,000 participants and 40 local and international Islamic scholars, marked the conclusion of an 11-day programme of hadith studies.
Yayasan Dakwah Islamiah Malaysia (Yadim) said this year's edition featured Jami' al-Tirmidhi and Syamā'il al-Muhammadiyyah, a collection of narrations describing the Prophet Muhammad's character and way of life.
The event also saw the launch of the 2026 National Pondok Umara' and Ulama' Muzakarah, aimed at discussing the future of traditional Islamic educational institutions and the development of Islamic education in Malaysia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Hour-long downpour sees UniSZA campus hit by flash floods
Article:
KUALA NERUS: An hour-long downpour caused several areas in Universiti Sultan Zainal Abidin (UniSZA) to be hit by flash floods this evening.
The flooding sparked concern among students as the main route back to their dormitories and the vehicle parking area began to be inundated.
Public Relations undergraduate Nurul Naziera Abdul Hafiz, 22, said she had to wade through floodwaters to return to her hostel after completing a group discussion with friends on campus.
"Although I was worried about having to walk through the floodwaters, I had no other choice but to return to my hostel.
"During last year's floods, I was fortunate enough to have returned to my hostel before the water started rising," she said.
Another student, 22-year-old Nur Ain Umairah Mat Nasir, said she and several others faced an alarming situation when they noticed floodwaters beginning to inundate the vehicle parking area.
"As soon as we stepped outside, we saw that the parking area was already beginning to flood, and everyone was rushing to move their vehicles to safer locations.
"The situation became more challenging as we had to move our motorcycles while floodwaters were rising quickly," she said.
She said, despite the flash floods, the situation remained under control, with the university management having a contingency plan in place to deal with the problem.
She added that her experiences dealing with floods in previous years had taught her how to respond appropriately.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
Article:
NVIDIA on Monday said it was reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO, effective immediately, an extraordinary reversal that followed calls from US President Donald Trump for his return after Huang resigned over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.
The reversal, which sent shares soaring 33 per cent, came after the board said it saw no national security risk in the return of Huang, who had also allegedly carried on affairs with at least two Nvidia employees.
Multiple investigations of the company are underway, including by the US SEC and the Department of Justice, related to everything from potential accounting issues to alleged chip smuggling.
Trump, who last week urged Nvidia to bring Huang back after its board ruled out his return, praised the reversal on Monday as the "correct and proper decision."
In a post on Truth Social, Trump said the US government had no reason to believe Huang's return posed a national security risk and had no evidence he had engaged in unlawful conduct.
He nevertheless urged Nvidia to continue investigating the company's compliance with US export controls to ensure it was meeting its obligations to protect national security.
Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones had said last week that the company would not rehire Huang despite a growing campaign for his return.
Huang resigned on Nov 12 following revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with a businesswoman whom US authorities suspect of spying for China, an allegation Beijing denies.
Huang built Nvidia from a video-game chip designer into the dominant supplier of artificial-intelligence processors, playing a central role in its chip roadmap, major customer relationships and ties with Washington.
Nvidia said its board voted unanimously on Monday to reinstate Huang after concluding that it was satisfied with his candour and leadership ability. The board said that, after receiving input from senior US government officials, it saw no national security risk from his return.
The board has also formed a committee to investigate whether foreign intelligence efforts targeted Huang and is also starting a search to name a new chief compliance officer. The company said Colette Kress would continue as chief financial officer.
Huang's departure reverberated from Silicon Valley to Taipei and Washington. A petition calling for his reinstatement drew more than 180,000 signatures, including one from Elon Musk, underscoring the unusually strong support for an executive who stepped down amid controversy.
The reversal highlights Huang's deep influence over Nvidia and raises broader questions about how dependent one of the world's most valuable companies remains on its co-founder.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MAHB says action taken after Sabah minister suffered head injury in KLIA
Article:
SEPANG: Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) has taken immediate action after a Sabah minister slipped and sustained a head injury at the VIP Lounge of Kuala Lumpur International Airport Terminal 1.
The airport operator said it regretted the incident and had taken follow-up action in response to feedback received from the passenger involved.
It said immediate medical assistance was also arranged for the guest shortly after the incident occurred.
"KLIA management has conducted a thorough inspection, and all necessary corrective measures have been fully implemented to ensure the safety of the facility," it said in a statement.
However, it did not specify the measures which were taken.
MAHB said it remained committed to ensuring a safe, secure and comfortable airport environment for all users across its facilities.
Earlier, the media reported that Sabah Agriculture, Fisheries and Food Industry Minister
Datuk Jamawi Jaafar sustained a head injury
requiring stitches after slipping in a toilet at KLIA this morning.
In a Facebook post today, Jamawi said the incident occurred when he slipped on the wet floor while using a toilet near the Bilik Bunga Mawar in KLIA's VIP waiting area.

Title: Mara orders probe after undercooked chicken served to MRSM students
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki has ordered a probe into claims that students at Maktab Rendah Sains Mara (MRSM) Tun Ghafar Baba in Melaka were served undercooked chicken.
The Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) chairman said he was angered and deeply concerned after receiving complaints from several students and parents through WhatsApp and private messages on social media about poor food quality.
The complaints, he said in a social media post, was on the food that was served to the students at the school's dining hall
Photographs accompanying his post on his Facebook page showed chicken that had not been properly cooked.
"I am extremely disappointed with the irresponsible attitude of contractors who behave this way," he said.
Asyraf said he had asked the school principal to investigate and take action immediately.
He added that checks revealed the food catering contract had only one month remaining, raising concerns that contractors might be neglecting food quality as their contracts approached expiry.
He said this appeared to be a recurring trend among food service contractors nearing the end of their contracts.
"I have also directed the Mara management, particularly its Secondary Education Division, to resolve the issue immediately," he said in the post.
Asyraf said he was concern about the welfare of students, many of whom could not afford to buy alternative meals from the school cafeteria or cooperative store.
He said the situation was particularly worrying for Form Five students sitting for the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia examination.
"Just a few weeks ago, I conducted a spot check at this MRSM and warned the dining hall supervisor to ensure that the quality of food served met Mara's standards," he said.
Asyraf said the contractor could face penalties and be blacklisted from receiving any benefits from Mara in the future.
"This concerns the welfare of students, and it is something I will not compromise on. Food contractors have a responsibility to ensure that the meals provided meet the standards set by Mara," he said.

Title: Anwar: Islam must never become a mask for corruption, oppression
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has warned against any attempt to allow Islam to become a mask for corruption, oppression and the marginalisation of the poor.
He said efforts to strengthen Islamic values must be accompanied by meaningful reforms to address wrongdoing and ensure that the poor and religious educational institutions are not neglected.
"Islam must not become a mask to legitimise misconduct, corruption and oppression while marginalising the poor," he said in his speech at the Khatam Sama' Hadis Antarabangsa 2026 ceremony at Masjid Putra.
Present were Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Datuk Dr Zulkifli Hasan and Grand Mufti of India Sheikh Abu Bakar Ahmad Al-Malibari.
Anwar said Malaysia continued to grapple with the legacy of colonial rule, which had transformed not only its political and educational systems but also the thinking and values of its people.
"After independence, the system changed, but colonial thinking was not necessarily eradicated. This is what we have inherited," he said.
Anwar said reversing the effects of colonialism and restoring Islamic consciousness required time, determination and a willingness to undertake reforms.
"That is why we have found the courage to bring about change. First, we must remember our history, and second, recognise that without inner strength, we cannot bring about any change," he said.
He also highlighted the historical role of madrasahs, tahfiz schools and pondok institutions in safeguarding Islamic teachings and preserving the community's identity during colonial rule.
Anwar said the government had been restoring financial support for these institutions over the past three to four years, with annual increases in allocations to upgrade facilities, some of which had fallen into disrepair.
He said Malaysia must also embrace emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence and digitalisation, without compromising its religious values, cultural identity and traditions, stressing that technological progress and major investments alone could not guarantee the nation's strength.
Under the 2027 Budget tabled last month, the government allocated RM200 million to repair and upgrade registered religious schools, tahfiz institutions and pondok schools, while expanding financial assistance to cover their operating costs.

Title: 'KLSCAH land premium reduction only controversial because FT minister is from DAP'
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The row over the Kuala Lumpur and Selangor Chinese Assembly Hall's (KLSCAH) reduced land premium would not have drawn the same scrutiny if the minister were not from DAP, says Hannah Yeoh.
The minister in the prime minister's department (federal territories) said the matter has drawn considerable attention because KLSCAH was a Chinese organisation and some people believed she had approved the land premium reduction.
"I believe with all my heart that if the federal territories minister were not me, from DAP, this matter would not have been brought into this (special) chamber. I am confident of this.
"During my 10-month tenure, whenever I spoke about valuable land in the Federal Territories, including open spaces, green areas and flood retention ponds, I stressed that we must defend and protect them.
"We have gazetted (many hectares) of land for protection, but they did not attract the same level of interest.
"But because this involves KLSCAH, a Chinese organisation, and a DAP minister whom they believe approved the reduction, there has been considerable interest," she said.
She said this when winding up the debate on an emergency motion concerning KLSCAH's land at the Special Chamber today.
Yeoh said land matters were governed by the National Land Code and fell under the jurisdiction of the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur Land Committee, chaired by the chief secretary to the government.
"I have no authority over this. I have no authority," she said.
On Nov 14, the government approved a 99-year lease renewal for KLSCAH at a nominal premium of RM1,000, compared with the initial estimate of RM4.67 million.
Yeoh had said on Nov 16 that the reduction took into account the change in the land's designated use from commercial to institutional.
She had said the land was restricted to institutional and heritage purposes, which were among the factors considered when assessing KLSCAH's appeal for a lower premium.
The Federal Territories Land Committee approved the surrender and re-alienation of the land for institutional use on Sept 14.
The decision has since prompted calls for greater transparency over the valuation process and the justification for the reduction.
The KLSCAH building was declared a National Heritage building in 2007, while the National Heritage Department allocated RM500,000 for conservation work in 2008.

Title: Pahang Sultan to open first ECRL station tomorrow
Article:
KUANTAN: The Sultan of Pahang will grace the opening of the KotaSAS central station, the first along the 665km East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) alignment tomorrow.
This comes ahead of the project's launching ceremony on Dec 12.
The KotaSAS station is one of 16 stations under the ECRL's first phase, running from Gombak Integrated Transport Terminal in Selangor to Kota Baru.
Notably, the station's project site was also the venue for the ECRL project's groundbreaking ceremony on Aug 9, 2017, by the then prime minister, Datuk Seri Najib Razak.
In a media invitation, project owner Malaysia Rail Link (MRL) said Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah would be accompanied by the Tengku Ampuan of Pahang, Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah, and the Tengku Mahkota of Pahang, Tengku Hassanal Ibrahim Alam Shah.
Chief Secretary to the Government and MRL chairman Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar and Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail are also expected to attend.
Following the opening ceremony, Al-Sultan Abdullah and the VIPs are expected to board the Comprehensive Inspection Train to the Bentong ECRL station before returning to KotaSAS.
The ECRL, which traverses Kelantan, Terengganu, Pahang and Selangor, is scheduled to begin operations next month, with ticket sales expected to open soon.
Pahang has seven stations along the alignment, namely Bentong, Kuantan Port City, Cherating, KotaSAS, Paya Besar, Maran, and Temerloh.
Terengganu has six stations in Jerteh, Bandar Permaisuri, Kuala Terengganu, Dungun, Kemasik and Chukai, while Kelantan has two in Kota Baru and Pasir Puteh.
Its extension from Gombak to Port Klang is expected to be operational by January 2028.

Title: Woman killed when SUV crashes into road divider
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A 25-year-old woman was killed after the Honda HR-V she was travelling in crashed into a road divider along Jalan Tuanku Abdul Halim on Friday.
The 3.42am accident occurred when the car, travelling from Damansara towards the Segambut roundabout, lost control while negotiating a bend.
Kuala Lumpur Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department deputy chief Superintendent Suffian Abdullah said the vehicle was driven by a 20-year-old man.
He said the driver sustained head and bodily injuries and was taken to Kuala Lumpur Hospital for treatment.
"The female passenger was pronounced dead at the scene," he said in a statement.
Suffian said an alcohol screening test could not be conducted on the driver as he was unconscious while receiving treatment.
However, blood and urine samples were taken for further analysis.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for causing death by driving recklessly or dangerously.
Anyone found guilty is liable to a jail term of between five and 10 years and a fine of between RM20,000 and RM50,000.
Those with information on the crash should contact the Tun H.S. Lee police station at 03-20719999 or any nearby police station.

Title: Myanmar woman risks all to bring 9-month-old into Malaysia, pays RM6,000
Article:
TUMPAT: Desperate to rebuild her life after her husband died, a 31-year-old Myanmar woman risked everything by bringing her 9-month-old daughter along on a dangerous journey into Malaysia.
The woman paid RM6,000 to a human trafficking agent to smuggle her and her baby into the country through the Thailand-Malaysia border.
However, their journey ended abruptly when they were arrested by General Operations Force policemen from the 7th Battalion during an operation yesterday.
The mother and her baby were among eight undocumented migrants detained in front of SK Neting, near Pengkalan Kubor, here.
The woman, who was planning to travel to Kuala Lumpur to look for work, intended to take a bus from Melor.
"I had to come to Malaysia to look for a job after my husband died," she said.
Despite the risks, she said she had chosen to bring her infant daughter along rather than leave her behind.
GOF Southeast Brigade commander Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the group had entered Kelantan from Tak Bai, Thailand, through Pantai Geting.
"They were travelling in a Perodua Myvi when arrested about 5am," he added.

Title: [UPDATED] KLSCAH land premium reduction done in accordance with KL land rules
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The reduction of the land premium to a nominal rate of RM1,000 for the Kuala Lumpur and Selangor Chinese Assembly Hall (KLSCAH) was made in accordance with the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur Land Rules 1995.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said the nominal rate was set after the land use condition for KLSCAH was amended to allow only institutional buildings, rather than commercial use.
She said the decision also took into account KLSCAH's agreement to convert the land tenure from leasehold to freehold, following its appeal for a reduction in the premium submitted on March 3.
She said the Kuala Lumpur Land Committee meeting on April 23 subsequently deferred consideration of the appeal and agreed that the Federal Territories Lands and Mines Office director should hold discussions with KLSCAH.
"Further discussions were held on June 9 to better understand KLSCAH's circumstances, given that its land is designated a National Heritage Site.
"KLSCAH subsequently expressed its intention to withdraw the appeal and submitted an application to surrender and realienate the land to enable it to be granted for use by a non-governmental organisation.
"In general, under land laws, the state authority has the power to consider applications for the surrender and realienation of land under Sections 197 and 76 of the National Land Code respectively.
"Through these two provisions, KLSCAH applied to convert the land tenure to freehold and amend the land-use condition to allow only institutional buildings," she said when winding up the debate on an emergency motion concerning KLSCAH's land in Special Chamber at the Dewan Rakyat today.
Yeoh said the nominal rate of RM1,000 "did not come from the sky or from assumptions", but was based on Rule 10 of the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur Land Rules 1995.
She said Rule 8C stipulates that land alienated for a place of worship is subject to a premium of RM3,000 per hectare or part thereof.
"The National Land Code and Rule 8C of the Federal Territory Land Rules clearly provide for this premium.
"Rule 8E stipulates that if the alienation is for public use by the federal government or an Islamic religious council, the premium is charged at the nominal rate of RM1,000 per lot," she said.
She also denied influencing the decision to change the land's status and reduce the premium, saying the KL Land Executive Committee made it.
"The chief secretary to the government chairs this meeting, not the federal territories minister from DAP, while the deputy senior secretary of the Prime Minister's Department serves as deputy chairman.
"The attorney-general, treasury secretary-general, Lands and Mines director-general, the Federal Territories Department director-general and the city mayor or their representatives, also sit on the committee.
"All of them are Malays. There is no one from DAP, and no Chinese, on the Land Committee that approved this (KLSCAH) application," she said.

Title: Bill on homeless expected to be tabled in 2028
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Women, Family and Community Development Ministry aims to table a bill specifically addressing homelessness by 2028 to tackle the issue more comprehensively and effectively.
Its minister, Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said the drafting of the proposed legislation was still at an early stage, with the ministry currently undertaking an in-depth study on the matter.
"God willing, perhaps in another two years or by 2028, we will have a bill on homelessness to be tabled.
"We are just starting out, and are now conducting research on this matter," she told reporters after attending a ministry gathering with media at Sultan Abdul Samad Building.
On the growing presence of foreign homeless people and beggars in the capital and across the country, Nancy stressed that the issue required inter-agency cooperation and was not the responsibility of any one ministry alone.
"When we conduct outreach operations, we work together with DBKL, the police and the Immigration Department to ensure that each agency and ministry addresses issues within its respective jurisdiction," she said.
Nancy also expressed her appreciation to media practitioners, describing them as an important bridge in conveying the latest information on the ministry's policies, services and new legislation to the public.
"Close cooperation between the ministry and the media creates a win-win situation that benefits not only the ministry but society as a whole," she said.
At the event, the Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama) received a Media Appreciation Award for its continued commitment to highlighting the voices of ministry's target groups.
The award was presented by Nancy to Bernama News Service Executive Editor Mohd Haikal Mohd Isa.

Title: KPJ Healthcare Q3 net profit rises to RM106mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: KPJ Healthcare Bhd's net profit for the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q3 2026) rose to RM106.31 million from RM93.91 million in the corresponding quarter last year.
Revenue for the quarter under review increased by 12 per cent to RM1.24 billion from RM1.11 billion previously, mainly driven by higher patient visits, an increase in surgeries performed and an improved case mix.
For the nine months, net profit increased to RM279.88 million from RM233.03 million, while revenue rose to RM3.49 billion from RM3.10 billion in the corresponding period last year.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, KPJ Healthcare said the group is well-positioned to navigate external headwinds, supported by its strong fundamentals and clear strategic direction.
"The group remains optimistic about its prospects for the current financial year ending Dec 31, 2026," it said.
Recently, KPJ launched its new flagship eye care centre, KPJ Centre for Sight PJ33, in Petaling Jaya, Selangor, and its first Orthopaedic and Rheumatology Centre of Excellence (CoE) at KPJ Penang Specialist Hospital.
"These will further enhance our specialised healthcare offerings and strengthen our position in providing comprehensive, high-quality services to Malaysians," it said.
KPJ's board of directors today approved an interim single-tier dividend of 1.20 sen per share for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026, amounting to RM53.1 million, payable on Dec 24, 2026.

Title: Berjaya Property's Q1 profit surges sevenfold to RM41mil on RM1.89bil revenue
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Berjaya Property Bhd's earnings surged sevenfold to RM41.02 million in the first quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 from RM5.53 million last year on the back of higher revenue.
Its revenue rose to RM1.89 billion in the quarter under review from RM1.88 billion a year ago.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said its improved performance was due to higher profit contribution from the property development and investment business segment in line with its higher revenue.
Other contributions include favourable foreign currency translation effect.
The higher revenue was mainly attributed to the higher revenue reported by the property development and investment business segment from development projects at Residensi Oak at Bukit Jalil, Pangsapuri Azalea at Subang Heights and Jesselton Courtyard at Jesselton Selatan, Penang.
These projects are progressing well as scheduled, coupled with increased revenue from its construction activities, Berjaya Property said.
The company said Malaysia's economic growth is expected to be driven by strong domestic demand and the moderation of the average inflation rate despite the uncertainties arising from ongoing geo-political tensions and conflicts as well as the inflationary effects of tariffs.
"The performance of the group's domestic business segments is expected to improve, supported by resilient consumer spending and the sustained growth in tourism activities, particularly in Malaysia under the extended Visit Malaysia campaign, which runs through year 2027," it said.
The group is looking forward to the completion and opening of the luxurious Four Seasons Resort & Private Residences Okinawa project in Japan in the fourth quarter of 2027, which will strengthen the performance of the hotels and resorts business segment.
The Four Seasons Okinawa is spread across 14 hectares of pristine beachfront paradise.
It will feature 279 exquisite accommodations including 127 resort rooms, 124 high-end condominiums, and 28 exclusive private villas.

Title: High tide phenomenon to hit Tumpat, Pengkalan Chepa hardest on Thursday, Friday
Article:

Title: What new Socso protection and incentives can gig, self-employed workers look forward to in 2027?
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 23 — An estimated 600,000 Malaysians earn a living through e-hailing and p-hailing.
However, unlike salaried employees, gig workers do not automatically receive the same employment-related social protection.
Budget 2027 proposes several measures to address this gap, including government-matched contributions to the Social Security Organisation (Socso) or Perkeso (Pertubuhan Keselamatan Sosial) as it is sometimes referred to; a package to raise workers’ net income and incentives to encourage retirement savings.
Some measures specifically target e-hailing drivers and p-hailing delivery workers, while others extend to self-employed people in sectors where Socso contributions are not compulsory.
If you are a gig worker or self-employed, here is how Socso could help.
What protection does Socso currently offer gig workers and the self-employed?
Socso’s Self-Employment Social Security Scheme, known as Lindung Kendiri, provides protection to eligible self-employed individuals against injuries arising from their work, including occupational diseases and accidents while carrying out work-related activities.
The scheme covers 20 sectors, including passenger transportation, goods and food delivery, agriculture, construction, manufacturing, hawking, online businesses and professional services.
For e-hailing and p-hailing workers, this means they can receive protection against work-related accidents while carrying out their jobs, subject to the scheme’s conditions.
Benefits include medical treatment, temporary and permanent disablement benefits, rehabilitation, dependants’ benefits and funeral assistance.
Unlike salaried employees, whose Socso contributions are deducted from their wages, self-employed workers register and pay contributions under Lindung Kendiri themselves.
However, contributions are mandatory for those working in the passenger transportation sector, including taxi, e-hailing and bus drivers, as well as the goods or food transportation sector.
The contribution amount depends on the insured monthly earnings category selected.
For example, the current contribution is RM13.10 a month for an insured monthly earning of RM1,050, RM36.90 for RM2,950 and RM49.40 for RM3,950.
What is new under Budget 2027?
The government has announced matching incentives to reduce the contribution burden for self-employed workers and encourage more people to obtain social protection.
This incentive can increase to 50 per cent if platform companies also contribute towards workers’ Socso contributions.
These measures are intended to make it more affordable for workers to contribute to Lindung Kendiri and obtain protection against work-related injuries.
What is the RM160 million package involving Grab?
Separately, the government and Grab Holdings Limited have agreed to share the cost of an RM160 million package for e-hailing and p-hailing workers.
The package will cover three areas: an increase in minimum income rates for e-hailing and p-hailing workers, assistance with vehicle maintenance and insurance costs, and Socso contributions.
This is intended to improve workers’ net income while strengthening measures to safeguard their welfare.
Under the projections announced in Budget 2027, median monthly net income for e-hailing drivers could increase by up to RM227, while p-hailing delivery workers could receive an increase of up to RM100 a month.
These are projected increases, not guaranteed monthly payments for every driver or rider.
The actual amount will depend on how the package and its income measures are implemented.
Who decides the minimum income rates for gig workers?
According to the Prime Minister’s Budget 2027 speech, the Gig Workers Consultative Council is negotiating a framework covering minimum income rates, the formula used to determine workers’ earnings and minimum standards of social protection.
The process is expected to be finalised in early 2027.
This is significant because gig workers’ earnings can vary according to factors such as the number of jobs completed, working hours and platform arrangements.
The proposed framework is intended to establish clearer standards for how workers are paid and protected.
Are there also incentives for retirement savings?
Yes.
Budget 2027 also provides for a matching incentive of up to RM600 a year for Employees Provident Fund (EPF) contributions by e-hailing drivers and p-hailing riders, subject to a lifetime limit of RM6,000.
The incentive is offered through i-Saraan Plus, an EPF voluntary contribution programme specifically for e-hailing and p-hailing drivers.
Under the programme, the government provides a 20 per cent matching incentive on eligible voluntary contributions, subject to the annual and lifetime limits.
This is separate from the Socso matching incentive.
While Lindung Kendiri provides protection against work-related injuries, EPF contributions are intended to help workers build savings for retirement.
Can gig workers claim tax relief on Socso contributions?
Budget 2027 proposes expanding tax relief for Socso contributions to include mandatory contributions under the Lindung Kendiri scheme.
Taxpayers will also be eligible for additional tax relief of up to RM150 for qualifying voluntary contributions to Lindung 24 Jam and Lindung Kendiri.
The proposed changes are intended to encourage more self-employed people to obtain social protection while providing some tax relief for their contributions.
What other assistance is available to gig workers?
Beyond social protection and income measures, Budget 2027 also includes financing facilities for gig workers who want to start a business or purchase their first home.
Bank Simpanan Nasional and Agrobank will provide a combined RM270 million in financing facilities for this purpose.
The government has also announced plans to introduce more comprehensive regulation of the p-hailing sector under the Land Public Transport Agency (APAD) and the Commercial Vehicles Licensing Board (LPKP).
These measures signal a broader effort to extend protections traditionally associated with formal employment to people earning a living through platform-based and self-employed work.

Title: Sigh of relief as flood evacuee numbers fall across Selangor and Perak
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 22 — Flood situations in Selangor and Perak continued to improve, with the number of evacuees at temporary relief centres declining to 2,151 people from 615 families this afternoon, compared with 2,315 people from 689 families this morning.
In SELANGOR, the number dropped to 1,727 people from 484 families, compared with 1,884 people from 532 families recorded this morning.
According to the Social Welfare Department’s (JKM) InfoBencana portal, the evacuees were housed at several relief centres, including Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Dato’ Maharaja Lela (397), SK Parit Mahang (360), Sekolah Rendah Agama (SRA) Bukit Kuching (180), Bukit Kuching Tengah Community Hall (135), SRA Batu 8 Ijok (120) and SK Rantau Panjang (four).
Other centres were SK Sultan Abdul Aziz (223 evacuees), SK Jaya Setia (73), Kafa Integrasi Hidayah Bukit Cherakah (65), Seri Harmoni Community Hall (36), SK Batu Arang (25), Balai Raya Kampung Sungai Kelambu (16) and SRA Pasangan (93).
In PERAK, the number of evacuees at five relief centres in four districts also dropped to 424 people from 131 families this afternoon, compared with 479 people from 157 families this morning.
The State Disaster Management Committee Secretariat said the SK Tanjung Belanja relief centre in Perak Tengah was closed at 2 pm after all 53 evacuees from 25 families were allowed to return home after floodwaters receded.
Meanwhile, SRA Rakyat Padang Serai in Manjung recorded 129 evacuees from 38 families, while the Teluk Intan Municipal Council Rest House Hall in Hilir Perak continued to house 97 people from 31 families.
In Kerian, the number of evacuees remained unchanged at 176 people from 55 families, including 12 landslide victims from three families, who were sheltering at SK Bukit Merah and SK Parit Haji Aman.
The number of flood evacuees in Larut, Matang and Selama also remained unchanged at 10 people from four families, housed at SK Batu Hampar. — Bernama

Title: ‘There are bound to be waves, but don’t sink the ship’ — Abang Jo tells GPS
Article:
KUCHING, Nov 22 — “Which sea is without rough waters? There are bound to be some waves, but do not sink the ship.”
This was the analogy used by Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) chairman Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg as he reminded the coalition’s component parties to remain united and avoid undermining their consensus ahead of the 13th Sarawak state election.
The Premier of Sarawak noted that differing views leading up to an election are to be expected, however, the entire machinery and crew must ensure that the GPS vessel continues to sail on the right course, guided by a spirit of camaraderie.
“During an election, all sorts of things happen. Which sea is without rough waters? There are bound to be some waves, but do not sink the ship. Let the ship, with its captain and crew, sail toward a glorious destination.
“The engines must be in good working order, and the technicians tending to them must be able to read the compass. If the compass isn’t set correctly, you’ll end up somewhere else. You need people who know how to read the ‘GPS compass’. We have a compass a ‘GPS’ compass crafted by Sarawakians so let us move forward,” he said, speaking metaphorically during the launch of the GPS election machinery at the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK) today.
Abang Johari, who is also the president of Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB), said the spirit of camaraderie rooted in firm mutual trust must be upheld to ensure political stability and the state’s development.
Earlier, the president of the Progressive Democratic Party (PDP), Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing, expressed his party’s intention to defend all eight state seats it held during the 13th Sarawak state election.
Tiong expressed confidence that the preparedness of the party’s election machinery, combined with the commitment of its entire leadership and membership, would ensure that all eight seats remain with the PDP within the GPS coalition.
GPS comprises PBB, Sarawak United Peoples’ Party (SUPP), Parti Rakyat Sarawak (PRS), and the PDP.
The Election Commission (EC) has set November 28 as nomination day, with early voting scheduled for December 8 and polling day for December 12. — Bernama

Title: Stay out of the water, Kelantan beachgoers warned as waves top 1.5-metre
Article:
TUMPAT, Nov 22 — Red flags have been hoisted at four popular beaches in Kelantan – Pantai Geting, Pantai Cahaya Bulan (PCB), Pantai Irama and Pantai Bisikan Bayu – due to rough sea conditions, with waves exceeding 1.5 metres high.
Kelantan Malaysian Civil Defence Force (APM) Deputy Director Lt Col (PA) Mohd Farid Ishak said the red flags, hoisted since Oct 27, warn the public against bathing or swimming at the affected beaches.
He said the rough sea conditions posed a drowning risk due to high waves and strong currents, including undertows, which could sweep people out to sea even when the water surface appeared calm.
“The public, particularly beachgoers, are advised against bathing or swimming in areas marked with red flags, as sea conditions are unsafe when waves exceed 1.5 metres high.
“Visitors should also always comply with instructions from the authorities and prioritise their own safety and that of their families,” he told Bernama recently.
Mohd Farid said the situation warranted serious attention as the country had entered the 2026/2027 Northeast Monsoon (MTL), which is expected to continue until March next year.
He said Kelantan was among the East Coast states at risk of prolonged heavy rain, strong winds and rough seas throughout the monsoon season.
According to the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), the early phase of the Northeast Monsoon, from November to January 2027, is expected to bring three to five episodes of continuous heavy rain, potentially causing floods in low-lying areas and locations near rivers.
Persistent strong northeasterly winds could also result in rough sea conditions and rising sea levels in the South China Sea.
Meanwhile, a Bernama survey at Pantai Geting found that some visitors were still bringing their families, including young children, to watch the waves, although they refrained from swimming or bathing.
Several APM personnel stationed at observation towers as lifeguards were also seen monitoring the area and advising visitors on the prevailing safety conditions. — Bernama

Title: Chow Kon Yeow rebuts Lim Guan Eng’s RM210m claim, says Penang won’t pay for undelivered water
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 22 — Penang is not required to make any payments to Perak before water supply under the Bulk Water Supply Agreement (BWSA) begins, Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said, dismissing claims that the state would have to pay RM210 million annually for 40 years despite receiving no water.
He said any payments under the agreement would also be subject to approval by the National Water Services Commission (SPAN).
“Therefore, the claim that the Penang Water Supply Corporation (PBAPP) must pay RM210 million annually for 40 years without receiving a single drop of water is misleading and unethical,” he said in a statement today.
Chow said the BWSA between Perak and Penang was an important agreement to secure the state’s water infrastructure capacity and supply security for the next 40 years, for the benefit of the people, industries, investors and future generations.
He said explanations on the agreement had been given repeatedly, but Bagan Member of Parliament Lim Guan Eng continued to allege that the process involved unethical practices.
“What is unethical about an agreement that guarantees infrastructure capacity and water supply security for 40 years?” he asked.
Chow, who is also PBAPP chairman and PBA Holdings Bhd (PBAHB) chairman, said the proposed BWSA had received approval from all PBAPP board members. PBAHB’s extraordinary general meeting (EGM) on Nov 12 also approved the proposal, with 98 per cent of shareholders voting in favour.
He said the professional views of PBAHB’s five independent directors had also been recorded and respected. The board approved the proposal by a majority vote of seven to five, with the five directors’ objections confined to certain payment terms, which had been addressed through specific clauses in the agreement.
Chow said the agreement would also give Penang access to substantial water infrastructure capacity without having to bear the full construction costs and initial development risks.
He added that PBAPP had contractual rights to take action, including invoking termination provisions, if any breach of obligations was not remedied in accordance with the agreement.
This meant Penang would not necessarily have to continue making payments until 2072, as alleged. — Bernama

Title: Anwar to host Lao deputy PM as Putrajaya, Vientiane seek closer economic ties
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 22 — Laos Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Thongsavan Phomvihane will undertake a three-day official visit to Malaysia beginning today as both countries mark 60 years of diplomatic relations.
In a statement on Sunday, the Foreign Ministry said Thongsavan is scheduled to pay a courtesy call on Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and hold bilateral talks with Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan in Kuala Lumpur.
“The meetings will enable both sides to take stock of the progress of bilateral cooperation, including in trade and investment, connectivity and transport, the halal industry, digital economy, capacity building, and exchange views on regional and international issues of common concern,” the statement read.
Both foreign ministers are also expected to sign a memorandum of understanding (MoU) on diplomatic training cooperation between Malaysia’s Institute of Diplomacy and Foreign Relations (IDFR) and Laos’ Institute of Foreign Affairs.
In 2025, bilateral trade between Malaysia and Laos increased by 157.8 per cent compared with the previous year, reaching RM258.4 million (US$60.7 million).
Malaysia’s exports to Laos amounted to RM77.7 million (US$18.2 million), while imports from Laos totalled RM180.7 million (US$42.6 million).
From January to August 2026, bilateral trade increased by 28.7 per cent compared with the same period in 2025, reaching RM225.3 million (US$55.9 million).
Malaysian investments in Laos include the 260-megawatt Don Sahong Hydropower Project in Champasak, Malaysia’s largest clean energy investment in the country. — Bernama

Title: Thunderstorm warning issued for parts of Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak until 8pm
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Nov 22 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning for several areas across Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak until 8pm today.
MetMalaysia said thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are expected in Perlis; parts of Kedah including Langkawi, Kubang Pasu, Padang Terap, Sik, Baling, Kota Setar and Pokok Sena; and several districts in Perak, namely Hulu Perak, Manjung, Perak Tengah, Hilir Perak, Bagan Datuk, Batang Padang, Muallim, Kinta and Kampar.
In Selangor, the affected areas are Kuala Langat, Klang, Kuala Selangor, Petaling and Sabak Bernam.
In Sarawak, the warning covers Kuching, Serian, Samarahan, Sibu, parts of Betong, Sarikei and Kapit divisions, as well as Tatau in Bintulu.
For Sabah, the warning is in effect for Beaufort, Sipitang and Tenom.
MetMalaysia said thunderstorm warnings are issued when there are indications of thunderstorms with rainfall intensity exceeding 20mm per hour that are imminent or expected to persist for more than an hour.
